owner_fcf_base: Normalized owner FCF base ~¥300bn (JPY). FY26 reported FCF was ¥262.6bn (margin 11.35%), but FY26 was an abnormal Switch 2 launch year (low margin on heavy HW mix, memory/component cost inflation, working-capital build). SBC is negligible for this Japanese issuer (sbc_pct_revenue/fcf null, treated as ~0), so Owner FCF = reported FCF with no SBC subtraction. Base normalizes mid-cycle between the FY26 trough (~¥263bn) and peak-Switch-era FCF (~¥450-550bn): conservador ¥270bn, base ¥300bn, optimista ¥330bn. Cross-checks vs FY26 record net profit ¥424bn (incl. ~¥44.3bn non-recurring FX gain) and FY27 guidance net profit ¥310bn (deliberately conservative: ~¥100bn memory/tariff headwind, assumes 150 JPY/USD).

assumptions.sbc_treatment: SBC treated as ~0 (negligible/undisclosed for this Japanese issuer); Owner FCF = reported FCF with full SBC expensing being immaterial. Net cash ~¥2,220bn (-$13.7B) added to equity value; ~¥1,909/share of IV is net cash alone.

conservador.note: Muted Switch 2 cycle, slower than Switch; persistent memory/tariff margin pressure; owner FCF base ¥270bn, Phase 1 CAGR 3.5%, decelerating to terminal g 2.5%. Still > current price because of low JP WACC and ¥1,909/sh net cash.

base.note: Switch 2 cycle echoes Switch success; digital/software mix and IP flywheel (movies, parks, mobile) lift margins; owner FCF base ¥300bn, Phase 1 CAGR 6% declining to terminal g 3.0%. Consistent with 37.8% ROIC and record FY26 track record.

optimista.note: Switch 2 outsells Switch, strong recurring digital + IP monetization, margin re-rating; owner FCF base ¥330bn, Phase 1 CAGR 8.5% declining to terminal g 3.5%. Perfect execution.

sanity_check: Stock is -52.7% off its ¥14,795 ATH (Aug-2025) and trades at fwd P/E ~19.9x vs a ~33x 10y trailing mean and ~25x est. 5y avg, i.e. a ~-20% discount. All three scenarios sit above ¥7,000; even the conservative case (¥10,200) implies meaningful undervaluation, driven by (a) Japan's low ~1.3% risk-free rate giving a 5.55% WACC and (b) ¥1,909/share of pure net cash (~¥2.22T, zero financial debt). Shareholder-return contrast (not DDM): FY26 dividend ¥219/sh = 3.1% yield; FY27 forecast dividend ¥162/sh = 2.3% yield; Nintendo also does opportunistic buybacks, so total shareholder yield is modestly above the dividend yield but is not the primary value driver here — the fortress net-cash balance sheet and IP-driven owner FCF are. Main risks to the thesis: console cyclicality / Switch 2 demand disappointment, JPY appreciation hitting overseas earnings, and the FY27 memory-cost/tariff headwind proving structural rather than transitory. TV weight is high (~79% base) — typical for a low-WACC, durable-IP compounder; conservative case explicitly haircuts growth and terminal g to test this.
method_notes: 10-year two-stage Owner Earnings DCF in JPY. Owner FCF = reported FCF minus 100% SBC; SBC is negligible for Nintendo so Owner FCF = reported FCF (no dilution adjustment needed — confirms R9 thesis). Base normalized owner FCF ¥300bn smooths the FY26 Switch 2 launch-year distortion (reported FCF ¥262.6bn at 11.35% margin). Phase 1 (yrs 1-5): explicit owner-FCF CAGR per scenario (cons 3.5% / base 6% / opt 8.5%). Phase 2 (yrs 6-10): CAGR declines linearly toward terminal g. Terminal value via Gordon growth at g (cons 2.5% / base 3.0% / opt 3.5%, justified by wide IP moat). Discounted at WACC = Rf 1.3% (Japan 10Y) + ERP 5.0% x beta 0.85; no geopolitical adjustment (Japan, not Taiwan). Equity value = PV of flows + net cash ¥2,220bn (net debt -$13.7B); IV/share = equity / 1.163B diluted shares. FX: ¥161.5/USD context only — all DCF math kept in JPY to match current_price. Probabilities sum to 1.00 (0.375 + 0.475 + 0.15).
